messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: high heap usage and repeated OOMs on hosted-runtime-gpupool-08 (>90% mem, 5 OOMs in 7m). Correlated service: kvcache-service. Pager routed to #incidents and @ben (oncall)

ben (oncall): getting eyes. is this customer impacting? any 5xx spikes?

caroline (support): yes — seeing ~2.3% 500 rate for text-gen endpoints in us-west-2 since ~08:12 UTC. Affected sessions show very long prompts (20k+ tokens).

alice (eng-runtime): sounds like continuous-batching + aggressive prefetch is pulling huge KV windows into memory. Recent rollout rolled batching_window_ms=60 -> 200 and prefetch_depth=8 -> 32 at 07:50 UTC. rolling back patch ID: rb-2026-03-17-cfg canary still in progress.

maria (sre): tagging perf graphs: https://metrics.internal/graphs/kvcache_heap?start=07:30&end=09:00 — you can see exponential growth on session-shard-12 around 08:05.

ben (oncall): severity? customer impact approx? need mitigation steps asap.

alice (eng-runtime): severity P1. Impact: small percent of requests erroring, but sustained OOMs risk broader pool outage. Immediate mitigation options:
- rollback batching_window_ms + prefetch_depth to previous values (quickest)
- set per-session kvcache token cap (e.g., kvcache_max_session_tokens=32768)
- enable eviction-by-age for sessions > N seconds
- fallback routing for long prompts to lightweight model variant (costlier but safe)

caroline (support): I can draft a customer note if we have ETA.

ben (oncall): do the rollback. alice, can you cut a hotfix? i'll coordinate pool-side restarts with ops. maria, prepare capacity to drain traffic.

alice (eng-runtime): on it. patching config now and will deploy to gpupool-* first. using admin API:  

```
# rollback batching/prefetch via admin
curl -X POST "https://admin.internal/config/reload" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"feature_flags": {"continuous_batching": {"batching_window_ms": 60, "prefetch_depth": 8}}}'
```

alice (eng-runtime): deployed config to gpupool-08 canary. monitoring logs.

incident-bot: Deploy event: cfg-revert-rb-2026-03-17 by alice at 08:34 UTC.

maria (sre): started rolling restart for kvcache-service on gpupool-08 nodes to force eviction of oversized sessions. rolling with 1 node at a time.

ben (oncall): observation?

alice (eng-runtime): canary looks good: heap dropped from 94% -> 48% on gpupool-08-canary within 90s. OOMs stopped in canary. planning full rollout to remaining nodes.

caroline (support): customer impact reduced. 500 rate dropping to 0.3% in us-west-2. I'll send interim note: "We observed transient errors from long-context requests; mitigation underway; we'll follow up with root cause and postmortem."

ben (oncall): roll the config to rest of pool. please include session cap change as additional guard after rollout.

alice (eng-runtime): applying session cap via admin:  

```
curl -X PATCH "https://admin.internal/config/kv" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"kvcache_max_session_tokens": 32768, "eviction_policy": "age_and_size"}'
```

alice (eng-runtime): session caps live across gpupool. monitoring.

maria (sre): monitoring shows stable heap, no new OOMs for 12 minutes. cluster healthy.

ben (oncall): good work. ownership:
- alice: follow up postmortem + revert validation (eng-runtime)
- maria: confirm no residual customer impact after 1h (sre)
- caroline: draft customer comms and coordinate with sales if any paying customers were affected (support)

alice (eng-runtime): logging notes for postmortem: correlate huge prompt length + continuous batching prefetched many KV pages; bug: prefetch did not bound by session token count when batching_window_ms increased. Will add unit test and config guard.

caroline (support): queued customer note, will circulate before 09:30 UTC.

maria (sre): creating incident ticket INC-2026-0317-KVCACHE for follow-up. collecting heap dumps and tracer logs.

ben (oncall): handing off to alice and maria for postmortem. I'll be available for comms if needed. Closing live pager in 30m if stable. :thumbsup:

alice (eng-runtime): thanks — will post RCA and timeline in this thread once complete.

incident-bot: Pager closed by ben at 08:59 UTC (duration: 27m).
